questions.stem: In a lesson on counting, for a deeper check, reason through this case: For 8 input bits, how many assignments make the parity (the XOR of all bits) equal to one?

options.misconception: it counts all assignments regardless of parity
it adds one extra assignment
it counts bits instead of assignments

questions.explanation: Exactly half of the 2 to the power 8 bit strings have odd parity, so the number with parity one is 128. Choice B is a distractor: it counts all assignments regardless of parity. Choice C is a distractor: it adds one extra assignment. Choice D is a distractor: it counts bits instead of assignments.
questions.hint: Half of all bit strings have odd parity.

questions.hint: By symmetry half of all assignments have a majority of ones.
